title: Chartbeat 2 billion visits and below-the-fold attention
statement:
Chartbeat's analysis of about 2 billion visits, mostly to media and news sites, found roughly 66% of attention on a normal media page was spent below the fold, so on content-led pages where the opening earns interest, sections below the fold deserve real design investment rather than being treated as dead space.

Options:
- Earn the scroll: Compelling first screen that gives a clear reason to scroll, followed by deeper sections that keep holding attention (fits: storytelling, editorial, warm)
- Substantive lower sections: Below-the-fold sections that continue the story with substantive content instead of filler or branding-only bands (fits: authoritative, informative, trustworthy)
- Measure your own scroll depth: Check scroll-depth and engagement analytics on your own page before deciding where the main CTA goes, because this data covers article pages, not landing pages (fits: data-driven, practical, technical)
- Long-form with anchors: Long-form scroll with anchored sections for content-led or story-driven products (fits: editorial, premium, calm)
appliesWhen: Applies to: media publishing. Audience: general.

source.title: What You Think You Know About the Web Is Wrong
